questions.q: Which three elements does the author say form charisma?
questions.why: The book lists presence, power, and warmth as key factors for charisma.

questions.q: What style of charisma focuses on fully attending to the other person?
a: Focus charisma, exemplified by Bill Clinton
Visionary charisma, exemplified by Steve Jobs
Kindness charisma, exemplified by Mother Teresa
Authority charisma, exemplified by Winston Churchill
questions.why: Focus charisma is described as being fully present on the other person, with Bill Clinton as an example.

questions.q: According to the text, what internal obstacle can damage charisma?
questions.why: Self‑doubt is listed among mental states that destroy charisma.

questions.q: What tool does the author suggest to reduce internal drama?
a: Dedramatize and see situations as less serious
questions.why: The first tool mentioned is to dedramatize and realize situations aren't as serious.

questions.q: Why is warmth important when combined with power?
a: It shows how power will be used, making the person likable
It hides the power's true intent
It replaces the need for presence
questions.why: Warmth signals how power will be applied, increasing likability.
